public_rationale: OpenAI brought the SearchGPT experience into ChatGPT, but the retrieved records do not establish search-specific profit or loss. Product availability, financing, and company-wide performance cannot settle this claim. There is no deadline, and the accounting basis is unspecified.
limitations: Failure to locate public product accounts is not evidence that the product is unprofitable.
Bundling search with other ChatGPT features makes revenue and cost allocation material.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Zitron doesn't think OpenAI will make SearchGPT profitable at all.

statement.excerpt: In fact, I don’t think you’re gonna make it profitable at all!

from_speaker: you’re gonna make it profitable at all
our_interpretation: The context identifies the product as OpenAI's search offering, initially called SearchGPT.
The ordinary reading is that this search offering will never generate positive product-level profit after attributable costs.
A successor integrated into ChatGPT remains within scope if it carries forward the search offering.
‘I don’t think’ expresses the speaker's confidence, rather than an external condition.
No accounting standard, cost-allocation method, or deadline is specified.
criteria.support_condition: A permanent end to the search offering, together with credible lifetime product accounts showing that it never became profitable, would support the forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible product-level accounts show positive profit for the search offering over a stated reporting period, including a defensible allocation of its costs.
